description: A ten by sixteen grid of coloured pixels running an arcade invader animation; four gate inputs drive it, and it has no audio of any kind

params.text: Sets how bright the pixels are and how slowly a pixel fades once it is drawn: turned down the trail is short, turned up it is long and the brightest pixels are pushed past full
Sets the hue the invaders are drawn in, once round the colour wheel across the travel; the four invader shapes are offset from one another so they never share a colour

inputs.text: A rising edge past 1V moves the whole fleet one pixel sideways and flips the invaders to their other animation frame; every 64 edges the fleet turns round and steps one pixel vertically
A rising edge past 1V fires a laser upward from a column picked at random along the bottom; the invader it strikes turns pale for about a fifth of a second
A rising edge past 1V inverts the bright pixels and washes the whole screen towards white for eight frames
Held above 1V, doubles the size of the picture and follows the fleet sideways; the laser and the flash are switched off for as long as it is held

notes: the module has no outputs and makes no sound. It is a picture, driven by the four gate inputs.
the screen is redrawn a hundred times a second, but the invaders only move when an edge arrives at jack 1. With nothing patched the same frozen fleet is drawn over and over.
the four jacks are numbered 1 to 4 on the panel. The maker's wiki calls them Walk, Fire, Crash and Zoom in that order.
all four jacks are read only once every hundredth of a second, so a trigger that rises and falls inside 10ms can be missed altogether.
the 160 pixels are lights rather than controls, so no click on the screen reaches help for anything.
